multi-tenancy.md: "There is often some level of trust between members of different teams, but Kubernetes policies such as RBAC, quotas, and network policies are essential to safely and fairly share clusters." and "The benefit of stronger tenant isolation must be evaluated against the cost and complexity of managing multiple clusters."
Conditional reasoning stated with its conditions (other site, own control plane, traffic can move, data present); 'can fail together' is hedged. No version-dependent behaviour; no doc governs it.

README: you "can share the same sealing key among a few clusters so that you can apply exactly the same sealed secret in multiple clusters." With claim 9 (only the holder of the private key decrypts), a leaked shared key opens every cluster's SealedSecrets; separate keys require sealing per cluster.

"the kubelet and (unless using virtual control planes) the API service are still shared services". issues.text: New in round 2. I can picture nodes kept for one customer, but no lesson I know says a cluster can set nodes aside, so this half-sentence answers an objection I had not raised. The point (the API server is still shared) is clear; I paused only to wonder whether I missed a mechanism.
issues.quote: nodes set aside inside one cluster still share its API server
issues.fix: Write 'even if some nodes were kept for that customer alone, they would still share the cluster's API server', so it reads as a hypothetical rather than a known feature.
